input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale:
Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated sum payable by the Company (our client, the customer) to HDI, so the rule is engaged in the flagged direction. The planner hint of "likelyAbsent" was incorrect: although the document uses no "liquidated damages" label, the Termination Payment is functionally a Customer-payable liquidated amount.

It breaches the preferred position (no LD or penalty payable by Customer) and reaches the walk-away threshold on quantum. Fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, whereas the Termination Payment is 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — a bill that exceeds a full year of actual fees (e.g. at $2m Net Sales: fees ~$560k/yr versus a ~$600k termination payment), and so exceeds remaining contract value. It is also triggered by any Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice under Section 4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach (only the narrow Section 1.6 late-launch right is expressly "without penalty"). The arrangement is one-way: Section 4.1 lets HDI walk on the same 90 days' notice for nothing, and p0028 confirms HDI never pays the Company.

I proposed the fallback rather than outright deletion because Section 1.2 has HDI bearing all Site design, development, hosting and promotion costs, recouping only through the revenue share, so some early-termination compensation is part of the genuine bargain and pure deletion would be disproportionate. The redline therefore caps the payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees, makes it the sole monetary remedy, and disapplies it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6.

ops.oldText: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement for convenience pursuant to Section 4.1, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment (the "Termination Payment") in an amount equal to the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI under Section 3.1 in respect of the three (3) calendar months immediately preceding the Termination Date. The Termination Payment shall be HDI's sole and exclusive monetary remedy in respect of such termination, and no Termination Payment, penalty, liquidated damages or other stipulated amount shall be payable by the Company where the Company terminates this Agreement as a result of HDI's breach of this Agreement or pursuant to Section 1.6.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Company, so we have replaced the Termination Payment formula (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) with our fallback cap of three months' fees under Section 3.1. Recognising that HDI bears the Site development costs under Section 1.2, we are content to leave a capped early-termination fee, but it must be the sole remedy and cannot be triggered where we terminate for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6.
proposal.summary: Cap the Customer-payable Termination Payment at three months' fees and disapply it on termination for HDI's breach.
